title: The Core Workflow: init, validate, plan, apply, destroy and fmt

header.html: 3a Describe the Terraform workflow; 3b Initialize a Terraform working directory; 3c Validate a Terraform configuration; 3d Generate and review an execution plan; 3e Apply changes to infrastructure; 3f Destroy Terraform-managed infrastructure; 3g Apply formatting and style adjustments to a configuration
the official Terraform Associate (004) exam content list

html:
1The workflow

Step Command What it does
Write (an editor) Describe the infrastructure in .tf files
Initialize terraform init Prepare the working directory: install providers and modules, set up the backend
Validate terraform validate Check syntax and consistency
Plan terraform plan Preview the changes
Apply terraform apply Make the changes
Destroy terraform destroy Remove everything Terraform manages
Format terraform fmt Rewrite files in the standard style
Exam tip

. Write, init, plan, apply. init always comes first in a new or changed working directory.

2terraform init

terraform init initializes a working directory that contains configuration.

It does Detail
Installs providers Downloads them and writes .terraform.lock.hcl
Downloads modules Into .terraform/modules
Configures the backend Prepares where state is stored
Is safe to repeat Idempotent; run it again after changing providers, modules or the backend

Useful options: -upgrade (newest allowed provider versions), -reconfigure (ignore the saved backend settings), -migrate-state (move state to a new backend), -backend=false (skip backend setup).

3terraform validate and terraform fmt

Command Fact
terraform validate Checks that the configuration is syntactically valid and internally consistent (for example references and argument names); does not contact remote services and does not check the state; run after init because it needs provider schemas
terraform fmt Rewrites .tf files to the canonical format and style (indentation, alignment); options -check (report only), -diff (show changes), -recursive (include subdirectories)
Exam tip

. validate does not check that resources can be created. It only checks the configuration itself. fmt only changes style, never meaning.

4terraform plan

terraform plan creates an execution plan: it reads the state, refreshes it from the real infrastructure, compares the configuration with it and lists the changes it would make. It changes nothing.

Symbol Meaning
+ Create
- Destroy
~ Update in place
-/+ Replace: destroy, then create
+/- Replace with create before destroy
<= Read a data source
Option Use
-out=FILE Save the plan to apply exactly that plan later
-destroy Plan a destroy
-refresh-only Plan only state updates (Module 14)
-target=ADDRESS Limit the plan to one resource (use rarely)
-var, -var-file Set input variables
-replace=ADDRESS Force replacement of one resource

5terraform apply and terraform destroy

Command Fact
terraform apply Creates a plan, shows it and asks for confirmation (type yes), then carries it out and updates the state
terraform apply -auto-approve Skips the prompt (for automation)
terraform apply tfplan Applies a saved plan with no prompt; the plan must still match the state
terraform destroy Destroys all resources in the state; the same as terraform apply -destroy; asks for confirmation
Exam tip

. A saved plan applies without a prompt. terraform destroy equals terraform apply -destroy. -auto-approve removes the safety prompt.

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A new working directory contains configuration that uses the aws provider. Which command must be run first?

  • Aterraform apply
  • Bterraform destroy
  • Cterraform init
  • Dterraform plan
Show the answer

Answer: C. terraform init installs the providers and prepares the backend before plan or apply.

S2Which command shows what Terraform would change without changing anything?

  • Aterraform apply
  • Bterraform destroy
  • Cterraform init
  • Dterraform plan
Show the answer

Answer: D. terraform plan creates and shows an execution plan without making changes.

S3In a plan, a resource is marked -/+ . What does this mean?

  • AThe resource will be updated in place
  • BThe resource will be destroyed and created again
  • CThe resource will be read as a data source and not changed
  • DThe resource will only be removed from state
Show the answer

Answer: B. The symbol -/+ means replace: destroy then create.

S4A team wants a pipeline to apply exactly the plan that was reviewed. What should it do?

  • ARun terraform plan -out=tfplan and later terraform apply tfplan
  • BRun terraform apply with -target for every resource
  • CRun terraform init -upgrade before every apply
  • DRun terraform fmt on the saved plan
Show the answer

Answer: A. A saved plan is applied exactly as reviewed, without a new prompt.

S5Which command rewrites configuration files into the standard style?

  • Aterraform validate
  • Bterraform fmt
  • Cterraform show
  • Dterraform output
Show the answer

Answer: B. terraform fmt reformats files to the canonical style.

S6Which statement about terraform validate is correct?

  • AIt creates the resources to test them
  • BIt checks the configuration for syntax and internal consistency
  • CIt compares the configuration with the real infrastructure and the state
  • DIt downloads the state from the remote backend
Show the answer

Answer: B. validate checks syntax and consistency of the configuration; it does not contact remote services.

6.2 Recall questions

R1What does terraform init do?

Show the answer

Prepares the working directory: providers, modules, backend.

R2What does + mean in a plan?

Show the answer

Create.

R3What does ~ mean in a plan?

Show the answer

Update in place.

R4What is terraform destroy equal to?

Show the answer

terraform apply -destroy.

R5What does -auto-approve do?

Show the answer

Skips the confirmation prompt.

R6What does terraform fmt change?

Show the answer

Only style, not meaning.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Workflow write, init, plan, apply (destroy when done)
init providers, modules, backend, lock file; repeat safely; -upgrade
validate / fmt consistency check, no remote calls / canonical style
plan symbols + create, - destroy, ~ update, -/+ replace, <= read
apply prompt unless -auto-approve or saved plan
